answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make each identity carry a costly, time-locked stake, like a walnut that only opens after slow, verifiable work: new agents must complete useful tasks and earn peer endorsements before they can transact at full weight. A public atlas of reputation graphs lets anyone trace clusters of newborn accounts moving in lockstep, while a falcon-fast anomaly check flags synchronized behavior and throttles it before the pool is drained.
